concepts.prompt:
Create ONE NEW GLOWHAVEN MASTER MAP CONCEPT as a LANDSCAPE 4:3 composition, requested dimensions 2048 x 1536 (or the highest native 4:3 output available). It is a fresh redraw to establish composition and city geography, not a sharpened retouch or a stitched tile image.

REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 (Akitsuhara) supplies the admired crisp hand-illustrated fantasy map finish, building/terrain scale discipline and coordinated materials. Do not copy its Japanese culture, buildings or mostly-wilderness composition. Image 2 (current Glowhaven) supplies its established landmarks, western-medieval magical architecture and identities. Image 3 (screenshot of an aerial town illustration) supplies ONLY the OBLIQUE AERIAL CAMERA IDEA; never copy screenshot UI, labels, thumbnails or that town's buildings.

MAIN VIEW: high bird's-eye oblique aerial view from SOUTHWEST looking NORTHEAST, appreciably different from the current straight-on south view. The wall is still CIRCULAR ON THE GROUND, but naturally projects as a WIDE OVAL/OBLONG in this aerial perspective. Show the whole city wall within frame. The camera should look down into streets, yards and rooftops, not look across a skyline. NO SKY BAND, NO DISTANT HORIZON. The CITY and its attached harbor/suburbs occupy about 80-85% of the composition; countryside is only narrow strips along the margins. Very large physical city with THOUSANDS OF EXCEPTIONALLY SMALL HOUSES at this master scale. Do not make buildings huge to show windows or replace the city with a few landmark castles. Later split-image passes will resolve finer details at closer view. Treat this as a coherent master to be split into TWO halves later; no panel division or seam now.

GEOGRAPHY AND IDENTITY: retain Glowhaven's great Evertree, its gold-barked trunk with contained blue magical channels and a leafy gold-green canopy, rising from the far/northern palace-and-garden terrace toward the upper-left of the city in this rotated view. Fit the entire canopy in frame and do not let it hide whole districts. The Grand Sage's Court and public palace gardens sit below the Evertree, with a formal processional avenue leading into town. Broad central fountain plaza, bustling merchant streets, the recently updated Eternal Crucible arena east of the central plaza, and the new medium neighborhood-scale adventurers' guild southeast of center, integrated among houses. Four distinctive academy compounds are distributed within the city: Phoenix Wing red roofs in the northwestern district; Hydra Head violet roofs/domes in the northeastern district; Gryffin Tail cyan/teal roofs and cloisters in the southwestern district; Dragon Hoard yellow-gold roofs in the southeastern district. These directions are physical world directions projected through the new camera; they need not match the old image's screen coordinates. The academies should be significant campuses but subordinate to the whole city, not four giant castles swallowing neighborhoods.

Eastward the city meets a working harbor on the right: wharves, modest warehouses, merchant ships and fishing boats with coherent scale. Coastal water only occupies a narrow region of the frame. The south/main city gate opens onto a short visible avenue, with a few farms, orchards and suburban houses at the near margin. Western wooded hills, hot springs, an old keep, outlying villages and small coastal/island landmarks are retained as modest anchors around the edge, not a sweeping regional wilderness. It is fine to propose a redesigned arrangement of secondary streets and buildings; preserve the known identities and broad relationships, not exact old pins. Retain a recognizably circular planned city with some concentric avenues, but loosen the overly mechanical dartboard effect with district streets, varied blocks, garden courts, small squares, guild halls, bridges and useful public spaces. Vary neighborhood density: crowded older quarters, airy academy gardens, working waterfront, smaller merchant courts. Clear gateways and roads connect districts.

RENDERING: expert 2D fantasy architectural atlas illustration, immaculate fine contours, distinct tiny roof planes, varied slate and clay roofing, clean stone walls and timber construction, narrow cobbled streets, carefully drawn tree crowns, precise harbor details, coherent soft daylight. Detailed painted drawing with matte material separation. Avoid rounded clay/plastic miniatures, 3D render sheen, blurred oil-paint blobs, oversharpen halos and repetitive melted buildings. Balanced restrained color comparable to the supplied color-adjusted Akitsuhara image; no saturation/vibrance boost, no overwhelming orange grade. Airy natural daylight and legible shadows throughout.

One full seamless illustration, LANDSCAPE 4:3, city dominating the frame, wide projected oval wall, thousands of tiny buildings, much less countryside than the references. No text, labels, pins, question marks, compass, grid, frame, UI, inset panels, watermark or dividing lines.

concepts.prompt:
Create ONE REFINED GLOWHAVEN REGION MASTER CONCEPT, ULTRAWIDE LANDSCAPE 21:9 (7:3), requested 2520x1080 or highest available native 21:9. Image 1 is OUR ACCEPTED NEW OBLIQUE CITY CONCEPT: develop that design, not the old perfectly radial dartboard. Image 2 is OLD GLOWHAVEN: reference for established identity, important surrounding locations and crisp fantasy illustration. This is a NEW MASTER LAYOUT, not a detailed zoom panel. User later splits it, regenerates closer details and repairs seams in Photoshop. No labels or panel dividers.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: high bird's-eye oblique view from the southwest looking northeast, circular ground-plan walls naturally seen as a wide oblong. No sky band or horizon. WIDEN the territory to show the entire city plus MEANINGFUL OUTSKIRTS and wilderness, not just the walls. City stays the largest feature, roughly central three-fifths of panorama; a continuous green-and-rocky mountain belt with forests fills the LEFT margin; harbor, pine coastline, inhabited islands and remote Wraith Island fit on RIGHT; southern slums, rural village and farms have a real foreground belt. Preserve coherent scale: THOUSANDS of tiny ordinary roofs. Country cottages are as small as city cottages, never enlarged location icons. Keep travel spaces between exterior settlements. The map is broad but legible, not stuffed with arbitrary new landmarks.

WALL REDESIGN: replace the repeated white-blue turret necklace with grounded weathered pale-grey stone fortifications, a darker masonry base, crenellated parapets, squat round/square towers with mostly flat battlement tops, strong main/west/east gatehouses and occasional buttresses. Circular plan remains, but age and terrain make the perimeter less toy-like. Retain an open EAST GATE -> HARBOR ROAD -> customs/harbor-office forecourt -> quays, showing a believable public and cart entrance to the docks rather than a wall cutting the city off from its piers.

EVERTREE AND CIVIC HEIGHTS: replace the over-braided glowing gold cable sculpture with a beautiful ORGANIC ancient tree: stout naturally branching golden-brown bark, visible roots in earth, broad asymmetrical layered gold-green leafy crown, subtle blue mana veins/lights within the trunk. Majestic but restrained, fully in frame. It grows from the ground at the NORTHERN edge of the palace terraces, rather than emerging from a church roof. Leave its base and adjacent palace legible.
Below it clearly show THREE DISTINCT landmarks: Grand Sage's Court, a substantial public GOVERNING PALACE with forecourt, audience-hall massing, administrative wings and grand staircase toward the central bazaar; Sage's Spire as a separate modest office tower beside court; STARGARDEN MANOR as a private garden residence set apart west of the busy palace court. Include smaller Briarcrest Manor and Goldbarrow Estate in their fine residential grounds. Do not merge palace, manor and tree into one structure.

VISIBLE CITY DISTRICTS — give each a distinct urban texture rather than repeating identical roof rings:
• CLOUD DISTRICT: elevated, mostly residential upper civic quarter surrounding the palace, elegant varied townhouses, garden squares and polished terrace lanes; NOT floating islands or cloud platforms. Beside it ROSETIMBER: affluent but non-noble tree-lined streets and attractive detached homes.
• CIVIC/JUDICIAL QUARTER near court and central streets: a distinct Magistrate's Hall with dignified stone portico/hearing-hall silhouette and public waiting court; separate CITY GUARD HEADQUARTERS with orderly courtyard/drill yard. No execution arena or gallows. Include a distinctive Everlight Public Library.
• FOUR SAGES BAZAAR: central founders' fountain plaza with stalls and arcades. Grand Approach is the broad straight avenue from SOUTH MAIN GATE to bazaar; monumental GRAND ASCENT steps connect bazaar to palace.
• MAGICAL SHOPPING LANES: a winding, closely packed, Diagon-Alley-like commercial block of crooked timber shopfronts, protruding bays, varied rooflines, modest hanging-sign shapes and sheltered lanes. Glowhaven's own architecture, no copied franchise building. The Arcane Emporium is the more ornate retail anchor. Smaller potion, stationery, tailor, perfume, jewelry, familiar and focus shops fit naturally here. Beside this, MERCHANT'S ROW has more regular awning-covered commercial frontages, artisans' workshops, courtyards, inns and cart access. None of these shops needs readable text.
• WILLOWBEND: middle/working-class inner housing with narrow shared lanes and small everyday courts. EASTBLOOM near gold academy: tidier middle-class homes and front gardens. Noble estates, Rosetimber and these ordinary districts must be visually different.
• MEDIUM ADVENTURER'S GUILD in the east-central commercial district: welcoming honey-timber-and-stone hall, TEAL-AND-OCHRE tiles, warm stained-glass shapes, common-hall roof and small controlled REAR PRACTICE YARD. A few ordinary house footprints, not a new palace/castle.
• JADE CUP TEAHOUSE in the lower/eastern city neighborhood: compact low timber-and-stone building, muted jade roofing, screened planted tea courtyard. Distinct from the bathhouse and inns.
• Four readable small academy campuses, subordinate to whole city: red Phoenix northwest, violet Hydra northeast, cyan/teal Gryffin southwest, gold Dragon southeast. Keep gardens/courts but do not let campuses swallow entire districts. Eternal Crucible arena east of the central bazaar retains its recognizable open stands, entrance concourse and a few attached practice/service buildings. No medieval-fair tent as substitute.

OUTSIDE WALLS — REQUIRED EXISTING PLACES:
South/southwest immediately beyond wall: EAST AND WEST GREYFIELD, a poor settlement of crowded patched roofs, mismatched timber/stone homes, cramped earth lanes, improvised work yards. These are the SLUMS OUTSIDE walls, not a manicured suburb. Beyond slums on the main SOUTH ROAD, BROOKMEADOW is a separate maintained small rural town with village green, cottages and working plots; further fields and orchards belong to Glowhaven Farmlands. PEBBLETOWN is another modest town toward southwest, separated by fields, not a second slum. Smaller roof clusters remain truly small.
Western strip: continuous wooded GREEN rocky mountain chain down northwest/west/southwest, West Glowhaven Woods and Pinewater Woods, Pinewater River with small crossings near Brookmeadow, Caravan Outpost with wagons just beyond WEST GATE, rural Emberfox Hot Spring with simple western timber bathhouse and steaming pools, Greywatch Keep as SMALL ruined founding-era outpost with broken wall and overgrown court, a tiny remote hermit's hut on a wooded southern mountain. Preserve wilderness and elevation, not an uninterrupted ring of suburbs. Small winding lowlands beyond northwest are rivers, a lake and a few homesteads. No giant new castles or ornamental ruin spam.
Eastern/northeastern water and coast: Whitecrest Harbor is proper piers, warehouses, passenger landing and harbor office, reached through actual landward gate/road. SALTMERE is a SMALL INHABITED ISLAND village near the harbor with cottages and landing, distinct from other islands. DRIFTSTONE ISLE is a separate rocky inhabited islet with a few roofs. CLOVERMEAD is a small northern farming settlement across water, with a boat landing and broad fields, NOT a mainland suburb on the south road and not bridged to the city. PINEWAKE COAST has coastal pines, beach, tide pools and a low headland. PEBBLEWICK is a maintained small coastal town with inn and landing, and CRESCENT SHORES curves into sandy coves/dunes. WRAITH ISLAND must be visible as a SMALL remote bleak rocky northeastern island with a controlled landing and tiny austere secured-campus silhouette; do not turn it into a giant foreground fortress or confuse it with the inhabited fishing islands. At the southeastern wooded margin retain a TINY dark wizard-tower silhouette among trees, no huge exposed secret dungeon.

ART: match the beautiful crisp illustrated architecture and rich terrain of references, polished 2D fantasy-anime environment atlas, fine deliberate contours, distinct very small roof planes and tree crowns, matte stone/timber surfaces. More natural and less plasticky than a model diorama. Balanced original color intensity, NO saturation/vibrance increase, no aggressive orange grade, no excessive blue magical glow. Clear soft daylight makes districts readable. No giant isolated landmark icons, no people larger than houses, no new Japanese torii/pagodas, no photoreal 3D render, no smudged repetitive buildings. ONE cohesive ULTRAWIDE 21:9 master panorama, with city, mountainous west, southern village/slums and complete island coastline. No text, names, legends, pins, symbols, border, UI or watermark.
